title: AWS CEO Matt Garman Defends Data Centers Amid Backlash: 'We Need To Be More Vocal'
source_used: Yahoo Finance (carrying Business Insider's story by Brent D. Griffiths; Benzinga page blocked, HTTP 403), cross-read against BigGo Finance
key_facts: Matt Garman, chief executive of Amazon Web Services (AWS), said in a recent interview on the 'A16z Show' podcast that Amazon needs to be more vocal and upfront about how data centres already affect daily life.
He said 'If you usually go to a community and say, "Do you not want to use Netflix?" They'll go, "No, no, I still want Netflix."'
He said 'I think we need to be more vocal and be more upfront because we actually do a ton that's really beneficial.'
Business Insider notes Netflix said in its 2025 annual report that it runs 'the vast majority of our computing on AWS'.

Garman said Amazon's development has benefited local tax bases and offered the example that residents might think differently if told 'your tax bill is $5,000 less than it would otherwise be if we weren't here'.
On 2 Oct he wrote that data-centre moratoriums could leave the US 'writing its own losing ticket' in the AI race.
A Fox News survey last month found 71% of registered voters oppose building a data centre in their area to support AI.
Business Insider says some state leaders are backing away from support for data centres as the issue becomes a political liability.
quote_evidence: "I think we need to be more vocal and be more upfront because we actually do a ton that's really beneficial," he said.
"If you usually go to a community and say, 'Do you not want to use Netflix?' They'll go, 'No, no, I still want Netflix,'" Garman said during a recent interview on the "A16z Show" podcast.
A Fox News survey conducted last month found that more than 7 out of 10 (71%) of registered voters said they opposed building a data center in their area to support AI development.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of Amazon's cloud business says the industry should answer public opposition to data centres by pointing to services and local taxes.
event_date: Podcast interview before 10 Oct 2026 (Business Insider piece dated 10 Oct 2026)
notes: Older news: the same a16z podcast interview was carried in our 10 Oct 2026 edition (Garman not worried about an AI bubble); the data-centre messaging remarks are the new angle.
